scope: Provisional chess judgements written from legal-looking boards and supplied continuations before engine/classifier output. Supplied motifs are not expected answers. Material, forced replies and pass counterfactuals still require verification.

cases.judgement: b5 cuts Qa4's diagonal protection of Nd7 while attacking the queen. Qg4 restores a different defensive diagonal, requiring f5 to cut it again. The two-step interference is more informative than a free-knight headline; every queen response and checking knight resource needs review.

Qg8+ Kh6 Qh8+ Kg5 Qxg7# appears forced. Mate should lead. At Kg5 the black king blocks its own Qg4 from recapturing on g7: useful secondary self-interference, not three new primary tactics. Check that this protection difference is real.

Be4 blocks Qc2's protection of Nf5 while attacking both queen and knight. The bishop's supported double attack and cut defensive ray belong to one combination. Interference seems the clearest main lesson if all replies lose material.

Rxc6 offers the exchange to remove the b7 pawn after bxc6. Bc7 then blocks Rd7's access to b7 and supports promotion. Black can decline the offer, so a source acceptance alone cannot prove the root sacrifice/deflection. The generic defensive-move tag is not an adequate explanation.

Kf3 presses the protected e3 pawn while White's other pawn moves are blocked or vulnerable. Suspect zugzwang, but b6 is a real pawn tempo and all king moves and the pass counterfactual must be checked. A king approach alone is not proof.

Kxf7 captures an unsupported knight. Qh5+ Kf8 shows that a check need not refute a material-winning king capture. Inspect Nd6+ and legal recaptures before assigning the net gain. Hanging knight is more concrete than defensiveMove.

Kc4 takes opposition and prepares queenside penetration and a5. The frozen kingside pawns make reserve tempi important. Test both turns and b4/c4 pawn breaks rather than equating opposition with zugzwang.

d4 exchanges the central pawn so Kxd4 can take opposition. A later h5 concession does not establish that the initial pawn move itself is zugzwang. Separate the central breakthrough/preparation from any verified reached zugzwang.

Kc5 constrains White, and Black spends a6/a5 as reserve tempi before d4 abandons c4's protection. Potential zugzwang and tempo play need an all-moves/pass comparison; do not borrow the final pawn capture as the first move's tactic.

Qa1+ exploits Ra8's x-ray through Ra2. Rxa1 vacates the a-file for Rxa1+, followed by Qb1 Rxb1#. Mate leads; x-ray support is a useful conditional secondary explanation. Check other interpositions and whether acceptance is forced.

Qxc2 exploits Rc8 behind Qc7: Qxc2 Rxc2 wins a rook net. The moved queen also attacks Qc7 and Rd1, so x-ray support and a double attack overlap. A hanging/free-rook headline misses why the recapture fails. Check Rd8+ and alternatives before ranking the mechanism.
Qxe1+ Rxe1 Rxe1# is a back-rank mate using Re8's x-ray through Re2. Mate/back-rank geometry should lead; the rook's x-ray support is secondary, not a separate free queen or rook gain.

Kf2 attacks Re3 and covers its e-file escapes. Rxe4 gives rook for knight; Rxd3 or Rxh3 loses the exchange differently. The trap should lead, with captured compensation deducted rather than claiming a free rook.

Bd4+ gains the tempo to play Be3, attacking Qh6 and closing its diagonal escapes. The queen has very limited mobility but the root is preparation, not the final trapping square. Every check evasion and queen interposition needs verification.
Ra8 attacks Qa5. Bishop and pawn coverage deny the escape squares; Qxc5 yields queen for bishop. Trapped Queen is the main cause, accounting for compensation and possible counterchecks.

a5 starts a passed-pawn race and White queens first, but Black's d-pawn can also promote. Being first alone does not prove a win. Check the resulting queen tactics and king alternatives; promotion belongs at its actual ply.
b8=N+ forks Ka6 and Qd7. Fork is the main tactical point; knight underpromotion is an important secondary action. Verify that queen/rook/bishop promotions are inferior before claiming necessity.

Rc6 attacks the blockading rook. Rxc6 abandons the b-file and allows b8=Q; rook retreats may instead permit an interference on b6. Verify all declines before claiming a root deflection or winning promotion.
